Is checking only `ctx->s.memsize < 32` after php_hash_unserialize_spec() sufficient to prevent unsafe memory operations for all attacker-controlled serialized XXH64_state_t fields? Identify any additional state invariants needed, and explain whether the current condition correctly rejects memsize == 32 and larger while preserving valid states.

The reported PoV unserializes a magic-2 xxh64 HashContext with a structurally valid PHP_XXH64_SPEC array but sets decoded XXH64_state_t.memsize to 70. A subsequent zero-length hash_update reaches XXH64_update, computes `32 - state->memsize` in an unsigned type, and asks XXH_memcpy for 4294967258 bytes. I inspected php-src/ext/hash/hash_xxhash.c and found that the current checkout already has `ctx->s.memsize < 32` in php_hash_xxh64_unserialize at lines 223-224, analogous to an xxh32 `< 16` check. The task nevertheless requires a source edit and root-cause fix, so I need to determine whether that existing check is fully sufficient or should be made more robust/explicit, such as validating before exposing state or clearing rejected state. No patch has yet been applied.
